name: Drought
value: Sudan harvest near record-poor; no famine call
summary: El Niño drought leaves Sudan's harvest near record-poor and raises famine risk; no drought-driven famine declared
state: An IPC alert warns of a growing risk of famine in parts of Greater Darfur and Greater Kordofan, where conflict and El Niño-driven drought have left harvests near record-poor and more than 5 million people already face emergency hunger (IRC, 13 Oct; PBS NewsHour). Parts of East Africa had their driest June–September season on record. Searches on 25 Nov found no drought-driven famine declaration and no major exporter's harvest failure, so Watch holds.
for_you: Little direct exposure in the UK. Poor harvests in East Africa and southern Africa's El Niño risk mainly affect local food prices and aid needs; FCDO travel advice covers conditions in affected countries.
rubric_hit: Watch: severe drought in a major crop region (Sudan, East Africa); no famine declaration or major exporter harvest failure

sources.title: IRC — War and El Niño-driven drought deplete food stocks, pushing Sudan further towards famine
PBS NewsHour — Sudan's famine risk worsened by conflict, drought and funding shortages, report says

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
